This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. - The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }

  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>

        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

2. **The target is parity** with what has worked before: heavy up-front intent clarification, then a one-shot build. That method works, but its up-front step is now beyond your threshold.

# Controlled vocabulary

The terms the harness uses with one fixed meaning. When a term here is used, it means exactly this and nothing looser. Entries are listed alphabetically.

## INDEX

> **Temporary home.** This entry is a file-tree convention rather than vocabulary, and will move once a better place for it exists. It sits here because there is none yet.

`INDEX.md` catalogues a directory of files: one line per file saying what it is and when to read it. A directory that holds subdirectories gets a `ROUTING_<DIR>` file instead.

- `_Backlog` holds ready items, moved there by `/sweep` and named `<prefix><YYYY-MM-DD>_<HHMMSS>.md`.
- `_Processed` holds items a later workflow has dealt with. `/sweep` never touches it.

## ROUTING_<DIR>

> **Temporary home.** This entry is a file-tree convention rather than vocabulary, and will move once a better place for it exists. It sits here because there is none yet.

`ROUTING_<DIR>.md` routes a directory of subdirectories: one entry per subdirectory saying what it holds and when to go there. `<DIR>` is the directory's name in capitals (`ROUTING_SYSTEM.md` in `System/`); the harness root's is `ROUTING_ROOT.md`. A directory that holds files gets an `INDEX` instead.

`ROUTING_ROOT.md` is pointed to only by the parent working directory, which uses it to manage the proper functioning of all System Components. System Components do not route through it.

## System Components

The child working directories that sit side by side at the harness root. Each has its own role and owns a set of system responsibilities that no other System Component shares. Each has its own `CLAUDE.md` for boot context, its own local skills, and a reading list drawing on both its own files and the parent's.

A System Component's fence is the smallest amount of access to the rest of the system it needs to carry out its responsibilities. It gets no more than that.

| System Component | Role |
|---|---|
| `Knowledge/` | Research and knowledge bases. Manages the Questions pipeline. |
| `Work/` | Creating outputs meant for external use. Manages the Ideas pipeline. |

`System/` is not a System Component. It is the parent directory's own file tree, has no `CLAUDE.md`, and is not a working directory.

Here's my first-cut design for the pipeline, then the weak points. I haven't researched anything for this; three claims below are marked unchecked.

**Recommended shape: one screen, one click**

1. **Draft as a single proposal card, shown in full in chat** (not a link). It has three parts:
   - the artifact text
   - where it would live
   - its retrieval trigger ("read when …")
2. **One click** with three options: Approve / Revise / Park. `AskUserQuestion` is the button; `process-problem` already uses it.
3. **On Approve, the assistant does the rest without asking again:**
   - writes the file and wraps it in `<operator_verified>`
   - adds the index line
   - adds the trigger
   - commits, quoting your answer in the commit message. That commit is the audit trail.
4. **On Park,** the card stays as a file in a drafts folder, so a later session can re-offer the same click. That keeps it pause-proof.

**Why location and trigger are part of what you approve:** a wrong trigger is exactly failure 6a/6b from the framework: either the artifact never gets read, or it gets over-applied. If you approve only the text, the riskiest decision skips your check.

**Your two open questions**

- **Length cap:** a word count is only a rough measure. What uses up your RAM is the number of separate things you have to check. Proposed starting values, to tune later:
  - one subject per artifact
  - at most 3 checkable claims
  - roughly 150 words or less
  - fits on one screen
  - anything bigger gets split into several cards, each with its own click

  Small, single-subject artifacts also keep their triggers narrow, which works against over-generalization.
- **Where the trigger lives:**
  - **The root reading list can't take it.** It sits inside `<operator_authored>` tags, so I can't add to it.
  - **The INDEX "Read when…" line already exists for this,** at the lowest folder. My default would be to reuse it.
  - **Its weakness:** retrieval depends on the model walking ROUTING → INDEX at the right moment, which is the same "not retrieved when the model makes decisions" failure you've already seen.
  - **Stronger options might exist** (all unchecked):
    - nested CLAUDE.md files that load when files in that folder are touched
    - path-scoped rule files in `.claude/rules/`
    - skill descriptions, which trigger on their own

**Where this breaks (adversarial)**

1. **I can fake approval.** Nothing technical stops me from writing `<operator_verified>` without your click. The protection is the rule plus the commit trail, and you'd only find a fake by checking. A hook might enforce it (unchecked).
2. **Drift after approval.** If I later edit text inside the tags, it's no longer what you approved. Proposed rule: any edit inside the tags removes them and sends the artifact back to draft.
3. **You have to write the rule yourself.** Your CLAUDE.md files currently say "never put those tags around the assistant's own text". The permission to add `<operator_verified>` after approval belongs in those operator-authored files, so you'd have to write that line.
4. **The click may not work in every session.** It may not be available in background or remote sessions like this one (unchecked; it isn't in my tool list right now). The Park-to-file fallback covers that.
